title: FluidFaaS: A Dynamic Pipelined Solution for Serverless Computing with Strong Isolation-based GPU Sharing
authors: Xinning Hui and Yuanchao Xu and Xipeng Shen
mechanism: MIG partitioned serverless functions with pipelined instance construction, eviction and dynamic resource assignment
environment: A100 80GB MIG profiles described; evaluation spans serverless deployment and GPU allocations. Per-GPU comparisons separated from aggregate system metrics; full driver/runtime settings not extracted.
workload: Image classification and depth recognition DNN function pipelines, light/medium/heavy invocation traces derived from Azure Functions; SLO set to 1.5 times isolated latency in default setup.
comparator: ESG MIG serverless baseline and INFless; baseline variants differ in pipeline execution.
finding: Section 7.1/Fig. 9 reports FluidFaaS SLO hit-rate improvement of 90% for medium and 61% for heavy workload mixes over the compared systems; the abstract reports 25–75% throughput increases across workloads. These are system-level results, not a measured per-GPU utilization effect.
limitation: Pipeline, placement and MIG allocation contribute jointly; comparisons with a non-pipelined baseline cannot isolate the benefit of MIG partitioning alone. No adversarial security or fault-injection evidence is inferred from MIG descriptions.
anchor: N00920.md abstract, sections 3, 6, 7.1; Tables 2, 5–6; Figs. 9 and 12
eligibility: Include: original HPDC full paper evaluates concurrent inference functions with local MIG partitioning and request SLO outcomes; separate server-level from local mechanism claims.

title: Improving GPU Sharing Performance through Adaptive Bubbleless Spatial-Temporal Sharing
authors: Shulai Zhang and Quan Chen and Weihao Cui and Han Zhao and Chunyu Xue and Zhen Zheng and Wei Lin and Minyi Guo
mechanism: Bless: adaptive kernel-squad scheduling, MPS contexts with SM affinity and temporal/spatial quota adjustments
environment: One A100 40GB (108 SM), AMD EPYC 7302, CUDA 11.8, Ubuntu 20.04 (section 6.1).
workload: Co-located inference and training DNNs; explicit two- and four-instance BERT inference scenarios and VGG11/ResNet50 quotas on one GPU.
comparator: Temporal round robin and quota-based spatial sharing/MPS configurations in section 6; relative percentages must retain their stated comparator and scenario.
finding: The introduction and evaluation report mean latency reductions of 39.1% for two BERT inference instances and 41.2% for four, under the paper's compared GPU-sharing systems. Other reported aggregate gains are not recast as p99 or universal speedups.
limitation: Quota, model pairing and GPU generation condition results. The conversion has damaged column/table layout, so no unlabeled plotted coordinates or precise tail-percentile gains were recovered.

title: Understanding GPU Resource Interference One Level Deeper
authors: Paul Elvinger and Foteini Strati and Natalie Enright Jerger and Ana Klimovic
mechanism: CUDA streams and CUDA Green Context SM partition for controlled co-location; interference characterization rather than a deployed scheduler
environment: H100 NVL (132 SM, CUDA 12.9, driver 575.57.08) and RTX 3090 (82 SM, CUDA 12.6, driver 560.35.03); modified vLLM fork.
workload: Llama 3.1 8B and Gemma 3 1B decode phases co-located with controlled sleep, copy or compute kernels; Table 1 H100 batch 8, 16,384-token prompt, ten generated tokens.
comparator: LLM decode alone versus controlled co-location in streams/Green Contexts; synthetic interference kernels, not a second production inference service.
finding: H100 Llama decode P90 time between tokens rises from 7.53 to 16.56 ms under a sleep co-tenant in section 4.2 (batch 1, 1,000-token prompt). Table 1's Green Context experiment isolates SM sets (64/68) but reports P90 TBT as high as 18.38 ms under copy-kernel memory pressure; its alone baseline is 14.2 ms on the whole GPU, so partition cost and interference cannot be collapsed into one effect.
limitation: Synthetic co-tenants and short decode traces quantify resource contention; the paper proposes a future scheduler but does not implement an end-to-end serving controller. Green Context SM partition does not partition L2 or external memory bandwidth. Table 1 conversion is interleaved; only prose and clearly attributable values are used.
anchor: N01096.md sections 3–5, especially 4.1–4.4; Fig. 2 and Table 1
eligibility: Include as direct interference/isolation evidence: real single-GPU LLM inference is concurrently run with a distinct synthetic process/kernel under streams and Green Context SM partition; a mixed co-tenant experiment is explicitly bounded, with no claim of two production inference services.
